name: Network Information (downlink, rtt, effectiveType)
plain: Reads estimated connection speed, type and latency.
meaning: Reveals if the person is on Wi-Fi, cellular or slow links; changes over time so useful for short term session linking.

limits.headline: Can see roughly how fast and what type your connection is, in Chrome and Edge
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads and while you stay on it
can: Check if your connection looks like Wi-Fi, cellular or slow
See rough speed and delay figures, rounded in coarse steps
Notice when your connection changes and use it to link short visits
Load lighter pages when your link is slow
cannot: See your exact speed or your provider
Work in Firefox or Safari, which do not offer it
See your name or location from this alone
Tell Wi-Fi from cellular in most cases outside Android
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet share it. Firefox and Safari, including all iPhone browsers, do not.

story.what_it_is: A page can read how fast and stable your connection seems to be, like Wi-Fi or slow 4G.

marketing.name: Network Information API
marketing.pitch: Pages can adapt to a slow or fast connection by reading its estimated type, speed and delay.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. If your signal is weak, a site may load smaller pictures or lower video quality without telling you. On a strong connection it shows the best version.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to adjust quality, skip heavy features and measure real world speeds across customers. The same numbers add a small clue to a browser fingerprint. Only Chromium browsers share them.

use_cases.example: A streaming site starts a video at lower quality when the reported speed is poor, so the first frame shows quickly instead of a spinner.
A browser 3D game picks smaller textures and fewer effects on a slow connection, so a player on a train can still load the level.
A store sends lighter product pictures to shoppers on slow mobile data, which keeps them from leaving before the page loads.
A performance dashboard groups page speed by reported connection type, to show how real customers on 3G and Wi-Fi are doing.
A news site turns off auto loading videos on slow lines to keep articles readable.
A web design tool such as Figma pauses background downloads of large files when the connection looks weak.
An ad script uses the connection type and speed with other values to build a fingerprint of a device.
